title: Review of c07's ringswim claim c1 (SIMD): on fresh seed 7 cells swim and divide until t~7400, then fuse into one domain-wrapping band to t=20000 (Weak)
summary: Fresh seed 7, labkit run of world_claim.py (T=20000, spf 100) plus c07's celltrack.py on world_claim.py and world_mu0.py. From noise, walled cells form by t~800 and swim as crescents with depletion wakes (celltrack: 11 track segments >= 3 BL, 6 >= 5 BL, best 19 BL; mu=0 twin: 0 >= 3 BL, best 1.8 BL), and divide: 17 splits, 8 persistent, max generation 4, all before t=7400. But merges (22) outnumber splits, and from t~6900 the cells line up and fuse into a single band that wraps the periodic domain by t~8700 and persists to t=20000 (rerun/seed7/sheet.png; labkit: 2 components final, 52 splits / 50 merges, 0 persistent splits). The claim's 'bounded population to t=20000 on all seeds' does not hold on seed 7; c07's README reports the same fate for the waste=0 arm on seed 1.

seeds_run.result: partial: swimming and 8 persistent splits (gen 4) before t=7400, then a single domain-wrapping band from t~8700 to 20000

verdicts.limitation: D is reticulate on this seed (22 merges vs 17 splits) and stops at t=7400 when the population fuses into one band; labkit's tracker finds 0 persistent splits. The long-lived 19 BL track 73 is largely the band-forming body, so it is not a cell that both swims and divides. One fresh seed; B not checked.
